name: Hollow Appendix
description: Hollow Appendix is a barren world with an impossible interior. Initial gravity surveys revealed that the planet is significantly less massive than its size suggests, and deep-penetrating scans confirmed the reason: the core is largely hollow, a vast spherical cavity roughly two thousand kilometers in diameter surrounded by a shell of dense rock and metal. The surface is a typical airless wasteland of impact craters and exposed rock, giving no external hint of the void beneath. Crystal cavern networks thread through the shell, connecting the surface to the hollow interior through narrow, winding passages.

The absence of atmosphere means the surface exists in vacuum silence, its cratered terrain baking and freezing in the cycle of day and night without any moderating influence. But instruments detect something unusual from the interior—faint gravitational anomalies that pulse in rhythmic patterns, as if the hollow space contains something that periodically shifts its mass distribution. The crystal caverns that penetrate the shell vibrate with these pulses, producing ultrasonic frequencies that can be felt through contact with the cavern walls even in vacuum.

The hollow interior is artificial. Scans at extreme resolution have revealed structural elements embedded in the shell's inner surface—the remains of a megastructure that once filled or lined the cavity, now largely collapsed or degraded. The exotic matter signatures emanating from the interior are consistent with advanced gravitational engineering, suggesting the hollow was created deliberately by a civilization with the ability to manipulate gravity on a planetary scale. The purpose of hollowing out a planet remains a subject of intense speculation.

Hollow Appendix has been designated a priority research site, but accessing the interior remains extraordinarily difficult. The crystal cavern passages are narrow, structurally unstable, and extend for hundreds of kilometers through solid rock before reaching the cavity. Remote drones sent through the passages have returned with imagery of a dark, spherical void whose inner surface is covered with the geometric remnants of the megastructure—and, in one image, what appears to be a single point of light at the exact center of the cavity, too small and too steady to be an instrument artifact. Something may still be operating in the dark at the heart of this hollowed world.
